2. Briefly stated, the facts are that the respondent No.2 Rupali Bank Ltd. Hazaribag Branch instituted Title Suit No. 47/1994 in the 4th Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka on 214.1994 which was transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka and re-numbered as Title Suit No. 214/1996, against the petitioner and others for realization of money amounting to Tk. 48,68,970.29 by selling the mortgaged property. The suit was decreed in preliminary form on contest on 1.6.97. The decree holder bank did not take any step immediately although the preliminary decree was sealed and signed on the same date. On 24.4.2003 the decree holder bank filed an application praying for an order making the preliminary decree dated 1.6.1997 final. The application was allowed by the learned Adalat and on the said date the final decree was sealed and signed. After the final decree was drawn up the respondent bank filed title execution case No. 114/2003 in the Court of Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka on 28.4.2003 against the petitioner. In the execution proceedings the Adalat issued proclamation of attachment against the Vs. Joint District Judge & Ors 15 BLT ( I-1CD )2007 petitioners, and the petitioner No. 2 informed by one of the officials of the respondent bank about the filing of the title execution case. It has been contended that the trial Court which was passed the preliminary decree had no lawful authority to draw final decree after the expiry of 3 years as provided under article 181 of the Schedule to be Limitation Act and consequently the order dated 24.4.2003 making the preliminary decree final is without any lawful authority. 

 3. The respondent No.2 Rupali Bank Ltd. has filed affidavit in opposition contending inter alia, that article 181 of the Schedule to this Limitation Act does not provide that after passing the preliminary decree the final decree shall have to be drawn up within 3 years from the date of preliminary decree and the Artha Rin Adalat on 24.4.2003 has drawn up the final decree in accordance with law and the final decree was put to execution decree within time. The petitioners remedy is not available under article 102 of the Constitution and as such the writ petition is not maintainable. 

 “Mr. Mesbahuddin has argued that since specific date was given in the preliminary decree with a direction for payment of the decreetal amount within 4(four) months, the right to apply to make the preliminary decree final accrued after the expiry of 4(four) months. The decree holder Bank having not applied for making the decree final within three years from the date when four months expired the application made by the decree holder bank ought not to have been entertained by the Adalat. The application was barred under Article 181 of the Limitation Act. Since the decree was sealed and signed on 1.6.97 and the decree holder bank made application on 24.4.2003 which is after more than 5 years the Adalat has no lawful authority to make the decree final as per the provision as laid down under Order 34 Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure as 3 years time as proved under Article 181 of the Limitation Act. He contends that time expired long before even the decree holder bank had not any legal right to apply to the Court for making the preliminary decree final after the expiry of the period prescribed by the law of limitation. The further contention raised by the learned Advocate is that since the order dated 24.4.2003 making the preliminary decree final was made beyond statutory period such decree is not executable and the title execution case No. 114 of 2003 is liable to be stuck down. 

 5. Article 181 as provided in the First Schedule Third Division of the Limitation Act is as under: 

 Description-of application 	    Period of limitation         Time from which period begins to run. 

 period of limitation is provided 

 6. Mr. Mesbahuddin has at least cited 2 decision of Indian jurisdiction on the proposition that the application should be filed within 3 years from the date when the right to apply accrued. One is the case of Mahamad Kamal Vs. Ahmed Ali and others reported in 87IC (1925)-746 and other case is Gajanan Chintaman Deshpande and others Vs. Karnatak Glass Industries and others reported in AIR 1971-Mysore, 241. The principle enunciated there is that the decree holders right to apply to make the preliminary decree final under order XXXIV rule 5 C, P. Code accrued after the expiry of the time given in the preliminary decree for payment of money and unless the application is made within 3 years from the dare when the right accrued the application would be barred under Article 181 of the Limitation Act. 

 7. Mr. Harunur Rashid the learned Advocate representing the Bank on the other hand contended that Article 181 of the Limitation Act has no manner of application and the Court which passed the preliminary decree had ample power to make the decree final even after the period of 3 years because the drawing up of final decree is a mere legal formality and the decree holder had the right to apply to the court to make the preliminary decree final at any time for the purpose of selling the mortgage property for satisfying the terms of the preliminary decree. There is no rule that the decree should be drawn up within 3 years. In support of his submission he cited a decision in the case of Chhaganlal Sakarlal Vani Vs. Jayaram Deoraj Thakar and others reported in 100 IC 956 which was decided in civil appellate jurisdiction where it has been stated that: 

 9.Overwhelming decisions of the- sub continental jurisdiction, particularly in the appellate, jurisdiction in a civil matter dealing with Order 34 Rule 5 and under section 181 of the Limitation Act, suggestion that in a Mortgage Suit where the order is made in the preliminary decree directing the judgment debtor to pay the decretal dues within certain specified dates and if payment is not made according to the direction and the time given, in that case the decree holder must make the applicable for making the preliminary decree final within 3 years after the expiry of that specified time, in other words the right to apply will accrue to the decree holder after the time given in the preliminary decree just passed. In the case of Cawnpore Municipal Board Vs. Pt. Tirjugi Narain reported in A.I.R.1947 Allahabad 82 (D.B) it has been observed that it is obvious that the application dated 24.4.2003 for the preparation of the final decree in accordance with the decree of this Court was beyond 3 years and was clearly barred by Article 181 Limitation Act 1908 similar view was expressed in the case of Bhajanmal Topandas and others Vs. Tikam das Thakurdas and others reported in A.I.R.1947 Sind 12. 

 10. We are not concerned with the proposition as to whether the provision of Order 34 Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure was wrongly or rightly applied by the Adalat in exercise of its power under the Code of Civil Procedure. The Adalat having' assumed jurisdiction under the Code of Civil Procedure may rightly or wrongly decide the question under the particular provision of law, but when the statute namely Limitation Act provides for and prescribes a time limit to do any act or pass any order under the Civil Procedure Code and the Court or Adalat does that act or pass any order going beyond that prescribed time limit that becomes without jurisdiction and Court having failed to exercise its power under Order 34 Rule 5 in making the preliminary decree dated 1.6.97 final within 3 years from the date when the right to make an application by the decree holder accrued, the impugned order dated 24.4.2003 appears to be without jurisdiction, because that order not only was passed beyond the statutory period but that also affected the rights of the parties, the judgment debtors. It is further noticeable from the impugned order that no notice was served upon the judgment debtor petitioner before making the preliminary decree final to hear the judgment debtor. In a writ of certiorari writ cannot issue to correct the mistake or wrong done in exercise of the power under the C.P. Code but in instance case the Artha Rin Adalat passed the impugned order and exercised its power going beyond the statutory period of limitation which cannot be otherwise excluded and as such the order is without jurisdiction and is liable to be struck down.
